name: Hilkiah
overview: Hilkiah was a male Levite who served as the high priest during the reign of King Josiah. As high priest, he was a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, which underscores his important role in leading Israel's worship and religious reforms during this period. His priestly office placed him at the center of spiritual leadership in Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Hilkiah means 'YHWH is [my] portion,' reflecting a personal acknowledgment of God's provision and sovereignty. This proper name, found in 2 Kings 22:4, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological implication in the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hilkiah as a descendant of Aaron, affirming his Levitical priestly lineage. It is also inferred that he was the father of the prophet Jeremiah, as noted in Jeremiah 1:1. Beyond these, the biblical record does not provide further details about his family relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Hilkiah's significance lies in his role as the high priest during King Josiah's reign, a time of major religious reform in Judah. His priestly office, rooted in the Aaronic line, positioned him to influence the spiritual direction of the nation. Through his leadership, he contributed to the rediscovery and restoration of the Law, which was pivotal in calling Israel back to covenant faithfulness.
